gloss: mastery through experience; learning by doing

definitions.gloss: mastery through experience; learning by doing
definitions.explanation: To truly understand or master something not through study alone but through personal experience and bodily practice. Implies deep, internalized understanding.

examples.japanese: {技術|ぎじゅつ}を{体得|たいとく}する。
examples.english: To master a skill through practice.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{経験|けいけん}で{体得|たいとく}したコツがある。
examples.english: There are tricks I've learned through years of experience.

examples.japanese: {料理|りょうり}の{基本|きほん}は{本|ほん}で{学|まな}ぶだけでなく、{実際|じっさい}に{作|つく}って{体得|たいとく}するのが{一番|いちばん}だ。
examples.english: The best way to learn the basics of cooking is not just from books, but by actually cooking and learning through experience.

notes:
USAGE:
Used with する to form a verb: {体得|たいとく}する. Emphasizes that the knowledge or skill has been internalized through practice rather than mere intellectual understanding.

WORD FORMATION:
{体|たい} (body) + {得|とく} (to gain). Literally 'to gain with the body,' reflecting the idea of embodied learning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {技術|ぎじゅつ}を{体得|たいとく}する (to master a technique)
- コツを{体得|たいとく}する (to learn the knack of something)
- {経験|けいけん}を{通|とお}じて{体得|たいとく}する (to learn through experience)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {習得|しゅうとく}: acquisition of a skill — more general, can include study
- {会得|えとく}: to grasp, to comprehend — focuses on understanding rather than physical mastery
- {身|み}に{付|つ}ける: to acquire, to learn — everyday expression for the same idea
